dossier.claim: Uncorrected word repetitions, misspellings, and fused words repeatedly interrupt otherwise recoverable passages. Their recurrence supports a proofreading problem without making every instance a new story error.
dossier.sourcePattern: The cited Japanese has no doubled conditional or doubled English verb, and the relevant names and actions are straightforward. The examples span domestic conversation, threats, combat, and magical training.
dossier.englishEffect: “Takes takes,” “making making,” “of of,” and “if you if you” remain in the text. “Thatit” loses a word boundary, “thorough” replaces “through,” “ringer” replaces “wringer,” and “Toshaka” misspells Tohsaka. These faults vary in severity, from visual interruption to selecting a different word.
dossier.limits: Deliberate repetition, speech disfluency, coined metaphors, and unusual sentence rhythm are not proofreading errors. Changes caused only by a damaged extraction are excluded. A typo may also belong to word choice or names, but overlapping tags do not turn it into multiple independent findings. Successful compact narration and source attribution remain relevant counterexamples.
